sources.scope: Original prompts, reference solutions and diagrams preserved. Numerical checks do not validate every source diagram or theorem proof.

LO01.title: Numerical expressions
LO01.prepare: Identify the words that determine the operation and group a whole sum or difference in parentheses before dividing.

LO02.title: Distributive Property
LO02.prepare: Distribute the outside factor to every term. Choose allowed test values to compare the original and expanded forms.

LO03.title: Addition and subtraction equations
LO03.prepare: Write the equation with one unknown X. Record the inverse operation you apply to both sides.

LO04.title: Rearrange formulas
LO04.prepare: Isolate the requested letter algebraically. Keep all nonzero-divisor restrictions; a numerical substitution checks only one instance.

LO05.title: Properties of equality
LO05.prepare: Identify the equality property from the structure: reversing sides, repeating an expression, or linking two equalities.

LO06.title: Variables on each side
LO06.prepare: Distribute first if necessary and collect unknown terms on one side. Enter the original equation as a check.

LO07.title: Distribute to evaluate
LO07.prepare: Group the terms exactly as stated and respect multiplication before addition. Retain parentheses around negative substitutions.

LO08.title: Rate of change
LO08.prepare: Label the two ordered pairs consistently. Use (second y − first y)/(second x − first x). For a prediction use the resulting rate and a known value.

LO09.title: Solve proportions
LO09.prepare: Match corresponding ratios. Keep variable denominators nonzero, then cross-multiply by hand.

LO10.title: Multi-step equations with parameters
LO10.prepare: Keep the parameter as a letter in the final formula. Choose an allowed nonzero value only for a numerical check.

LO11.title: Dilations of linear functions
LO11.prepare: Compare the coefficient of x with the parent y=x. Calculate sample outputs to support the stretch/compression description.

LO12.title: Slope-intercept form
LO12.prepare: Isolate y first. Divide every term by its coefficient; the x coefficient is the slope and the constant is the intercept.

LO13.title: Read linear graphs
LO13.prepare: Read two exact labelled points from the graph, respecting the axis scale. Compute slope, then b=y−mx. Do not estimate unlabelled coordinates.

LO14.title: Graph step functions
LO14.prepare: Apply the greatest-integer definition before arithmetic. Distinguish a value at an endpoint from values immediately to either side.

LO15.title: Slope from two points
LO15.prepare: Compute Δx and Δy in the same order. If Δx is zero, stop: a vertical slope is undefined.

LO16.title: Evaluate step functions
LO16.prepare: Subtract 1 from the given x, find the greatest integer no larger than that result, then multiply by 2. Rounding is not floor.

LO17.title: Arithmetic sequence arguments
LO17.prepare: Compare successive differences before using an arithmetic-sequence formula. A nonconstant difference invalidates that formula.

LO18.title: Constant linear functions
LO18.prepare: Read the constant height b. A horizontal line has equation y=b and slope zero; a table can confirm its constant outputs.

LO19.title: Verbal expressions
LO19.prepare: Identify the operation and the order of the operands from the expression. Arithmetic can illustrate the operation but cannot select its wording.

LO20.title: Solve multi-step equations
LO20.prepare: Write each inverse operation and preserve the equality. Use SOLVE on the original equation as a check.

LO21.title: Evaluate algebraic expressions
LO21.prepare: Substitute every supplied value in parentheses, then apply the order of operations.

LO22.title: Use and rearrange formulas
LO22.prepare: Write the formula, identify the units, substitute given values, then isolate the unknown before calculating.

LO23.title: Equations, identities and contradictions
LO23.prepare: Expand and collect terms first. A contradiction and an identity must be established algebraically; SOLVE cannot classify them reliably.

LO24.title: Graph with a table
LO24.prepare: Rearrange into y=f(x), choose the requested x values and generate the table. Transfer the pairs to a labelled graph.

LO25.title: Piecewise functions
LO25.prepare: Enter each piece separately with its own interval. Mark open/closed endpoints manually; TABLE does not enforce piecewise restrictions.

LO26.title: Arithmetic nth term
LO26.prepare: Identify a₁ and d, then write aₙ=a₁+(n−1)d. Substitute the requested index and keep its meaning in your answer.

solutions.text: Group the entire sum or difference before performing the stated multiplication or division.

setup: Use Calculate mode (MENU → Calculate on ClassWiz). Clear the previous entry with AC.
Use the (−) key for a negative number, √ for a square root, and the power key for an exponent. The → key exits a root or exponent template.
Keep exact values during the calculation. Use S⇔D to compare with a decimal; round only the final answer.

solutions.text: Add or subtract the same number on both sides to isolate the variable; substitute to check.

setup: Use Calculate mode. Use X in place of the problem’s unknown, and enter both sides of the equation.
Use ALPHA then CALC for the equality sign inside the equation; the ordinary = key evaluates an entry.
Press SHIFT then CALC (SOLVE). For this example enter the initial guess 0 and confirm. A different guess can fail or converge differently; never use a zero denominator.
Read X and the L−R residual. For these linear/rational equations check the result in the original equation and reject forbidden denominators.
G9G-BOOK-Q03-MCQ-01.interpret: Write the solution in the original variable. Include your inverse-operation or cross-multiplication steps and the substitution check; a SOLVE display is not the full written solution.

LO01.title: FOIL binomial products
LO01.prepare: Expand using all four products and combine like terms. A numerical check can detect a mistake but does not prove an identity.

LO02.title: Squares of sums and differences
LO02.prepare: Use (a±b)²=a²±2ab+b²; include the middle term and its sign.

LO03.title: Sum and difference products
LO03.prepare: Use (a+b)(a−b)=a²−b². A calculator check should evaluate both the product and proposed difference.

LO04.title: Factor using distribution
LO04.prepare: Find the greatest common factor and divide every term by it. Expand the result by hand to prove the factorisation.

LO05.title: Analyse monic trinomial factors
LO05.prepare: List integer factor pairs whose product is the constant and whose sum is the x coefficient. Calculator roots alone do not prove integer factorisation.

LO06.title: Factor non-monic trinomials
LO06.prepare: For ax²+bx+c, find integer factors of ac that add to b, split the middle term and factor by grouping.

LO07.title: Difference of squares
LO07.prepare: Identify both squares and use a²−b²=(a−b)(a+b). Keep any greatest common factor outside.

LO08.title: Divide monomials
LO08.prepare: Divide numerical coefficients and subtract exponents of like bases. State that each original denominator is nonzero.

LO09.title: Negative and zero exponents
LO09.prepare: Apply zero/negative exponent rules before evaluation. Put negative bases and fractional exponents in parentheses.

LO10.title: Rational exponents
LO10.prepare: Interpret a rational exponent as a root followed by a power. Keep the base domain and real-root restrictions.

LO11.title: Products of square roots
LO11.prepare: Multiply radicands and extract square factors. For geometry, set up the area or length formula first.

LO12.title: Quotients of radicals
LO12.prepare: Combine compatible radicals, simplify and rationalise if required. Preserve nonzero denominators and real domains.

LO13.title: Add and subtract radicals
LO13.prepare: Simplify each radical, then combine only like radical terms. A decimal is a check, not the requested exact surd.

LO14.title: Factoring in context
LO14.prepare: Translate the context or factorisation task first. For a quadratic equation, move all terms to one side and identify a, b and c.

LO15.title: Square root and completing-square methods
LO15.prepare: Follow the requested square-root or completing-square method. Use a polynomial solver to check every root, including a repeated root.

LO16.title: Translations of quadratics
LO16.prepare: Write the function as (x−h)²+k and identify (h,k). Use TABLE around x=h to confirm the vertex and symmetry.

LO17.title: Factoring quadratic equations
LO17.prepare: Write the equation as a product equal to zero and apply the zero-product property. Never divide by the variable and lose the zero solution.

LO18.title: Dilations and reflections of quadratics
LO18.prepare: Identify the outside multiplier and shifts in a(x−h)²+k. If the multiplier is inside a square, square it before describing the vertical effect.

LO19.title: Solve quadratics by graphing
LO19.prepare: Roots are x-intercepts, so set y=0. Read or estimate intercepts on the graph; use Polynomial as a numerical/exact check where an equation is given.

LO20.title: Complete the square
LO20.prepare: For a monic quadratic, halve the x coefficient and square the result. Add the same quantity to both sides of an equation.

LO21.title: Add and subtract polynomials
LO21.prepare: Combine like terms. When subtracting a polynomial, change the sign of every term in the second group.

LO22.title: Multiply polynomials
LO22.prepare: Distribute every term and combine like terms, then check the product at allowed numerical values.

LO23.title: Multiplication properties of exponents
LO23.prepare: Identify whether powers are multiplied or raised to another power. For area square the whole side; for volume cube the whole side.

LO24.title: Quadratic extrema and graph features
LO24.prepare: Read the vertex and y-intercept from the graph using its scale. Use the vertex x-coordinate for the symmetry axis and its y-coordinate for the extremum.

LO25.title: Write a quadratic from its graph
LO25.prepare: Read the vertex and another point, write y=a(x−h)²+k, and solve for a. Only then use TABLE to check the derived equation against the graph.

LO01.title: Polynomial operations
LO01.prepare: Order polynomial terms by descending powers; identify the coefficient of the leading term separately.

LO02.title: FOIL and binomial products
LO02.prepare: Expand every product or use the correct special-product identity, then combine like terms.

LO03.title: Factoring by GCF and grouping
LO03.prepare: Factor out a greatest common factor, or group terms to expose a shared binomial. Re-expand to verify.

LO04.title: Factoring monic trinomials
LO04.prepare: Find two integers with the required product and sum. Re-expand the factors to prove the result.

LO05.title: Interior angles of polygons
LO05.prepare: Use the interior-angle sum (n−2)×180°. Set up the equation before evaluating the unknown.

LO06.title: Properties of parallelograms
LO06.prepare: Use the marked parallelogram property to equate opposite sides/angles or supplement adjacent angles. Solve that equation before reporting a length.

LO07.title: Tests for parallelograms
LO07.prepare: Use the marked sufficient condition for a parallelogram. A drawing or numerical coincidence does not prove parallelism or congruence.

LO08.title: Kites
LO08.prepare: Identify the perpendicular diagonals and equal adjacent sides of the kite. Use angle sums or the Pythagorean theorem as appropriate.

LO09.title: Dilation coordinates
LO09.prepare: For a dilation about the origin multiply both coordinates by the same scale factor. Keep signs and vertex labels.

LO10.title: Similar polygons
LO10.prepare: Match corresponding sides in the correct order, form a proportion and solve it. Check the scale factor in a second pair.

LO11.title: Dilation scale factors
LO11.prepare: Divide image length by original length to find the dilation factor. Distinguish enlargement from reduction using its magnitude.

LO12.title: AA triangle similarity
LO12.prepare: Identify two corresponding equal angles. Calculate a missing angle using 180° only when the given angles support it; state AA in the proof.

LO13.title: Proportional parts in triangles
LO13.prepare: Identify corresponding proportional segments or a midsegment before setting up an equation. Do not compare noncorresponding lengths.

LO14.title: Parts of similar triangles
LO14.prepare: Use corresponding altitudes, medians or angle bisectors of similar triangles in the same ratio as corresponding sides.

LO15.title: Geometric mean
LO15.prepare: Draw the altitude/right-triangle relationships, identify the correct geometric-mean equation and then take the nonnegative length.

LO16.title: Pythagorean theorem and converse
LO16.prepare: Identify the longest side. For a right triangle use c²=a²+b²; for classification compare c² with a²+b² and verify a triangle exists.

LO17.title: Special right triangles
LO17.prepare: Use the exact side ratios of 45°–45°–90° or 30°–60°–90° triangles before calculating.

LO18.title: Right-triangle trigonometry
LO18.prepare: Label opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to the given angle. Set Degree mode and choose sin, cos or tan accordingly.

LO19.title: Angles of elevation and depression
LO19.prepare: Draw the horizontal reference line and right triangle. Account for observer height before using a trigonometric ratio.

LO20.title: Area with two sides and an angle
LO20.prepare: Use A=ab sin(C)/2 with the included angle C. Use Degree mode and keep full precision until the final unit-labelled area.

LO21.title: Special-product factorization
LO21.prepare: Choose the special-product pattern, retain common factors and expand by hand to verify.

LO22.title: Interior and exterior angle reasoning
LO22.prepare: Distinguish interior and exterior angles. Exterior angles total 360°; a regular polygon has equal exterior angles.

LO23.title: Solving with similar triangles
LO23.prepare: Prove similarity and write the ordered correspondence before forming a side proportion. Calculator arithmetic does not replace the proof.

LO24.title: Distance and midpoint in space
LO24.prepare: Use the three coordinate averages for the midpoint and the square root of the sum of three squared differences for distance.

LO25.title: Law of Sines and the ambiguous case
LO25.prepare: Use a/sin(A)=b/sin(B) in Degree mode. For SSA, test both B and 180°−B and retain only triangles whose angle sum is below 180°.

LO01.title: Dilation and scale factor
LO01.prepare: Image = scale factor × original coordinates (center at the origin). k>1 enlarges, 0<k<1 reduces. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO02.title: Proportions in similar polygons
LO02.prepare: Similar polygons have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO03.title: Triangle similarity by AA
LO03.prepare: Two pairs of equal angles are enough to prove two triangles similar (AA). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO04.title: Triangle similarity: AA, SSS and SAS
LO04.prepare: Choose AA, SSS or SAS: SSS needs three equal ratios, SAS needs two equal ratios with the included angle. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO05.title: Triangle similarity: AA, SSS and SAS
LO05.prepare: Use the similarity to write proportions between corresponding sides, then solve for the unknown. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO06.title: Proportional parts of triangles
LO06.prepare: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally; the converse also holds. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO07.title: Corresponding bisectors, altitudes and medians
LO07.prepare: In similar triangles, corresponding bisectors, altitudes and medians have the same ratio as the sides. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO08.title: Geometric mean
LO08.prepare: Geometric mean of a and b is √(ab). Altitude to the hypotenuse: h² = (segment 1)(segment 2). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO09.title: Pythagorean Theorem
LO09.prepare: In a right triangle a²+b²=c², where c is the hypotenuse. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO10.title: Applications of the Pythagorean Theorem
LO10.prepare: Draw the right triangle hidden in the situation, label legs and hypotenuse, then apply a²+b²=c². Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO11.title: Distance between points
LO11.prepare: d = √((x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO12.title: 45°–45°–90° triangles
LO12.prepare: Sides are in ratio 1 : 1 : √2. Hypotenuse = leg × √2. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO13.title: 30°–60°–90° triangles
LO13.prepare: Sides are in ratio 1 : √3 : 2 (short leg, long leg, hypotenuse). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO14.title: Trigonometric ratios: sides and angles
LO14.prepare: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent. Use the inverse key to find an angle. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO15.title: Trigonometric applications
LO15.prepare: Sketch the right triangle, choose the ratio that links the known and unknown sides, solve. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO16.title: Represent sample spaces
LO16.prepare: List all outcomes with a table, tree diagram or organised list. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO17.title: Fundamental Counting Principle
LO17.prepare: If choices are made in stages, multiply the number of options at each stage. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO18.title: Dependent and independent events
LO18.prepare: Independent: P(A and B)=P(A)·P(B). Dependent: P(A and B)=P(A)·P(B given A). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO19.title: Conditional probability
LO19.prepare: P(B | A) = P(A and B) / P(A). List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO20.title: Mutually and non-mutually exclusive events
LO20.prepare: Mutually exclusive: P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B). Otherwise subtract the overlap: P(A)+P(B)−P(A and B). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO21.title: Properties of similar polygons
LO21.prepare: Scale factor = ratio of corresponding sides; perimeters have the same ratio, areas the square of it. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO22.title: Proportional parts of triangles
LO22.prepare: Write the proportion of the divided sides and compare ratios to test parallelism. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO23.title: Trigonometric ratios: perimeter and area
LO23.prepare: Find missing sides with sin/cos/tan, then use P = sum of sides and A = ½·b·h. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO24.title: Angles of elevation and depression
LO24.prepare: Angles of elevation/depression are measured from the horizontal; draw the right triangle and use tan. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO25.title: Dependent and independent probabilities
LO25.prepare: Check whether the first draw changes the second: with replacement events are independent. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO26.title: Mutually and non-mutually exclusive probabilities
LO26.prepare: P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A and B); the overlap is 0 only for mutually exclusive events. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO01.title: Graph exponential growth functions
LO01.prepare: For y=a·bˣ with b>1 the graph rises, passes through (0,a) and has the x-axis as asymptote. Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO02.title: Solve exponential inequalities
LO02.prepare: Write both sides with the same base, then compare exponents (reverse the sign if 0<b<1). Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO03.title: Convert exponential and logarithmic forms
LO03.prepare: log_b a = c ⇔ bᶜ = a (b>0, b≠1, a>0). Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO04.title: Solve logarithmic equations using properties
LO04.prepare: Use log a + log b = log(ab), log a − log b = log(a/b), log aⁿ = n·log a, then remove the logs and check the domain. Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO05.title: Change of base formula
LO05.prepare: log_b a = log a / log b = ln a / ln b. Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO06.title: Natural base and natural logarithms
LO06.prepare: ln x is log base e; ln eˣ = x and e^(ln x) = x. Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO07.title: Simplify rational expressions
LO07.prepare: Factor numerator and denominator, cancel common factors, and state excluded values. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO08.title: Simplify complex algebraic fractions
LO08.prepare: Multiply numerator and denominator by the LCD of all inner fractions. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO09.title: Transformations of reciprocal functions
LO09.prepare: y = a/(x−h) + k: asymptotes x=h and y=k; a stretches/reflects. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO10.title: Solve rational equations
LO10.prepare: Multiply by the LCD, solve, then reject any root that makes a denominator zero. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO11.title: Classify types of statistical studies
LO11.prepare: Survey, observational study, experiment (treatments imposed), simulation: decide who assigns the treatment. This is a reasoning question: decide with the definitions, no calculation is needed.

LO12.title: Experimental and theoretical probabilities
LO12.prepare: Experimental = successes ÷ trials; theoretical = favourable outcomes ÷ all equally likely outcomes. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO13.title: Design probability simulations
LO13.prepare: Assign digits so the simulated chances match the real probabilities, then repeat many trials. List or count the outcomes first; use the calculator only for the arithmetic of the probabilities.

LO14.title: Distribution: center, spread and shape
LO14.prepare: Describe centre (mean/median), spread (range, IQR, SD) and shape (symmetric, skewed). Enter the data in STATISTICS and read the mean, deviation and quartiles; describe shape from the graph yourself.

LO15.title: Angles in standard position
LO15.prepare: Standard position: vertex at the origin, initial side on the positive x-axis; coterminal angles differ by 360°. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO16.title: Values of trigonometric ratios
LO16.prepare: Use the reference angle and the quadrant to find the value and sign of sin, cos, tan. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO17.title: Properties of periodic functions
LO17.prepare: Period, amplitude and midline: A = (max−min)/2, midline = (max+min)/2. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO18.title: Applications of sinusoidal functions
LO18.prepare: Model with y = A sin(B(x−C)) + D; period = 2π/B. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO19.title: Other trigonometric functions
LO19.prepare: csc = 1/sin, sec = 1/cos, cot = 1/tan; tan = sin/cos. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO20.title: Inverse trigonometric functions
LO20.prepare: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹ return an angle in the principal range: [−90°,90°], [0°,180°], (−90°,90°). Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO21.title: Evaluate expressions involving the natural base and logarithms
LO21.prepare: Domain of eˣ is ℝ, range (0,∞); average rate of change = (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a). Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO22.title: Exponential growth and decay using logarithms
LO22.prepare: Half-life T: k = ln 2 / T and y = a·e^(−kt). Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO23.title: Rational functions: oblique asymptotes and holes
LO23.prepare: Divide when deg(top) = deg(bottom)+1 to get the oblique asymptote; a cancelled factor gives a hole. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO24.title: Normal probabilities, areas and inverse values
LO24.prepare: z = (x−μ)/σ; use the table or normalcdf; Empirical Rule 68–95–99.7. Standardise z = (x−μ)/σ and read the area from the supplied table, or use Normal CD / Inverse Normal.

LO25.title: Degrees, radians, arc length and phase shifts
LO25.prepare: Arc length s = rθ (θ in radians); π rad = 180°; phase shift = C in A sin(B(x−C)). Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

operations.purpose: Average rate of change = (f(−2) − f(−5)) / 3 for f(x)=3e^(x−1)+3.

solutions.text: Domain R; range (3,∞); horizontal asymptote y=3. Average rate=e^(−3)−e^(−6)≈0.0473.
Included in the combined reference solution for part a.

setup: MENU → Calculate. For log_b(a) enter ln(a) ÷ ln(b) (or log(a) ÷ log(b)); require a>0, b>0, b≠1.

Keep full precision for decay constants; show the algebra and domain restrictions in the written answer.
11A-Q21-10.interpret: Matching values give a numerical check only; show the algebraic steps in your written solution.

LO01.title: Characteristics of quadratic graphs
LO01.prepare: y=ax²+bx+c: axis x=−b/(2a); vertex on the axis; a>0 opens up (minimum), a<0 down (maximum). Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO02.title: Graph quadratic functions
LO02.prepare: Plot the vertex, the y-intercept and a mirror point, then draw the parabola through them. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO03.title: Solve quadratics by graphing
LO03.prepare: The real solutions of ax²+bx+c=0 are the x-intercepts of the graph. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO04.title: Solve quadratics by factoring
LO04.prepare: Factor, then use the zero-product property: each factor = 0. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO05.title: Complete the square in an expression
LO05.prepare: x²+bx+(b/2)² = (x+b/2)². Add and subtract (b/2)². Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO06.title: Quadratic Formula
LO06.prepare: x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / (2a). Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO07.title: Discriminant and nature of roots
LO07.prepare: D=b²−4ac: D>0 two real roots, D=0 one repeated root, D<0 no real roots. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO08.title: Quadratic inequalities in two variables
LO08.prepare: Graph the boundary (dashed for < or >), then test a point to choose the shaded side. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO09.title: Evaluate and analyze polynomial functions
LO09.prepare: Substitute the value (or use synthetic substitution); the degree and leading coefficient give the shape. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO10.title: Power functions and end behavior
LO10.prepare: Even degree: both ends the same direction; odd degree: opposite directions. The sign of the leading coefficient sets which. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO11.title: Polynomial graphs and zeros
LO11.prepare: Real zeros are x-intercepts; a factor (x−c)ⁿ crosses at c if n is odd and touches if n is even. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO12.title: Relative maxima and minima
LO12.prepare: A relative maximum/minimum is a turning point where the graph changes direction. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO13.title: Polynomial long division
LO13.prepare: Divide the leading terms, multiply back, subtract, bring down; repeat. Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO14.title: Synthetic division
LO14.prepare: For divisor x−c use c with the coefficients: bring down, multiply by c, add. The last number is the remainder. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO15.title: Solve polynomial equations by factoring
LO15.prepare: Move everything to one side, factor completely (GCF, grouping), set each factor to zero. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO16.title: Exponential growth graphs
LO16.prepare: y=a·bˣ, b>1: a is the y-intercept and the x-axis is a horizontal asymptote. Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO17.title: Exponential growth and decay
LO17.prepare: y = a(1±r)ᵗ: growth uses 1+r, decay uses 1−r. Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO18.title: Types of statistical studies
LO18.prepare: Survey, observational study, experiment: an experiment assigns the treatment to subjects. This is a reasoning question: decide with the definitions, no calculation is needed.

LO19.title: Sampling and biased questions
LO19.prepare: A random sample represents the population; leading or loaded wording makes a question biased. This is a reasoning question: decide with the definitions, no calculation is needed.

LO20.title: Empirical Rule and normal areas
LO20.prepare: About 68%, 95%, 99.7% of data lie within 1, 2, 3 standard deviations of the mean. Standardise z = (x−μ)/σ and read the area from the supplied table, or use Normal CD / Inverse Normal.

LO21.title: Solve quadratics by completing the square
LO21.prepare: Move c, add (b/2)² to both sides, write (x+b/2)² = value, take square roots. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO22.title: Quadratic inequalities in one variable
LO22.prepare: Find the roots, split the number line, test a point in each interval. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO23.title: Add, subtract and multiply polynomials
LO23.prepare: Add/subtract like terms; multiply by distributing every term of one factor to the other. Rearrange to standard form first; the Equation/Func solver gives every root to check your factorisation or formula.

LO24.title: Solve exponential equations
LO24.prepare: Write both sides with the same base and equate the exponents. Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO25.title: Normal probabilities and inverse values
LO25.prepare: z=(x−μ)/σ; read the area from the table; for an inverse value reverse the process. Standardise z = (x−μ)/σ and read the area from the supplied table, or use Normal CD / Inverse Normal.

LO01.title: Estimate arc length
LO01.prepare: Approximate a curve by short straight segments and add their lengths; more segments give a better estimate. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO02.title: Limits algebraically and graphically
LO02.prepare: Evaluate by substitution, factoring/rationalising when 0/0, or read the value approached from the graph. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO03.title: Squeeze Theorem
LO03.prepare: If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) and lim g = lim h = L then lim f = L. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO04.title: Limit laws for polynomial, rational and trigonometric functions
LO04.prepare: Limits of sums, products and quotients are the sums, products and quotients of limits (denominator limit ≠ 0). Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO05.title: Continuity at a point
LO05.prepare: f is continuous at a if f(a) exists, lim f exists, and they are equal. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO06.title: Continuity of functions and compositions
LO06.prepare: Polynomials, rational functions (in their domain), trig and exponentials are continuous; compositions of continuous functions are continuous. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO07.title: Infinite limits and limits at infinity
LO07.prepare: Divide by the highest power of x to evaluate limits at infinity; a zero denominator with non-zero numerator gives ±∞. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO08.title: Average and instantaneous velocity
LO08.prepare: Average velocity = Δs/Δt; instantaneous velocity = lim of that as Δt→0 = s′(t). Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO09.title: Sketch a function from its derivative graph
LO09.prepare: f′>0 where f increases, f′<0 where f decreases, f′=0 at flat points. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO10.title: Derivative of a function at a point
LO10.prepare: f′(a) = lim (f(a+h)−f(a))/h, the slope of the tangent at x=a. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO11.title: Power Rule for derivatives
LO11.prepare: d/dx xⁿ = n·xⁿ⁻¹. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO12.title: Product and Quotient Rules
LO12.prepare: (fg)′=f′g+fg′; (f/g)′=(f′g−fg′)/g². Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO13.title: Chain Rule
LO13.prepare: (f(g(x)))′ = f′(g(x))·g′(x): differentiate the outside, keep the inside, multiply by the derivative of the inside. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO14.title: Derivative of an inverse function
LO14.prepare: (f⁻¹)′(b) = 1 / f′(a) where f(a)=b. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO15.title: Trigonometric derivatives
LO15.prepare: (sin x)′=cos x, (cos x)′=−sin x, (tan x)′=sec²x. Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO16.title: Exponential derivatives
LO16.prepare: (eˣ)′=eˣ; (aˣ)′=aˣ ln a. Rewrite with a common base when possible; otherwise take logarithms. Use the power key for evaluations.

LO17.title: Natural logarithmic derivatives
LO17.prepare: (ln x)′=1/x; (ln u)′=u′/u. Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO18.title: Implicit differentiation
LO18.prepare: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treat y as y(x) (multiply by dy/dx), then solve for dy/dx. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO19.title: Inverse trigonometric derivatives
LO19.prepare: (sin⁻¹x)′=1/√(1−x²), (cos⁻¹x)′=−1/√(1−x²), (tan⁻¹x)′=1/(1+x²). Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO20.title: Hypotheses of Rolle’s Theorem
LO20.prepare: Rolle: f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), f(a)=f(b) ⇒ f′(c)=0 for some c. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO21.title: Continuity: definition and applications
LO21.prepare: Choose constants so that the left limit, right limit and the value at the join are equal. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO22.title: Horizontal, vertical and oblique asymptotes
LO22.prepare: Vertical: zero of the denominator; horizontal/oblique: compare degrees at infinity. Decide the limit algebraically (substitute, factor, divide by the highest power); the calculator only shows the trend numerically.

LO23.title: Product Rule
LO23.prepare: (fg)′ = f′g + fg′. Simplify the result and evaluate at the requested point. Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

LO24.title: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
LO24.prepare: Combine trig derivatives with product/quotient/chain rules; tangent line: y−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a). Set the angle unit first, then use sin/cos/tan (SHIFT + key for the inverse). Keep full precision.

LO25.title: Applications of exponential and logarithmic derivatives
LO25.prepare: Differentiate the model, then interpret f′(a) as the instantaneous rate of change with units. Use ln for base e and ln(a) ÷ ln(b) for log base b. Check the domain by hand first.

LO26.title: Mean Value Theorem
LO26.prepare: MVT: f′(c) = (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a) for some c in (a,b) when f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b). Differentiate by hand with the rules; the calculator can check a derivative value at a point.

solutions.text: Reviewed answer key. A written step-by-step solution has not been transcribed for this source card; use the lesson rule and the calculator guide.

setup: MENU → Calculate. Type f(x) with the x variable, then press CALC and enter values such as a ± 0.001 from both sides.
Both one-sided trends must agree; a calculator table is evidence, not proof.
For limits at infinity evaluate at large values of x (for example 10⁶) to see the trend.
12A-p14-Q10-1.interpret: Write the method, the substitution and the final answer with units. Calculator output alone does not justify the answer.

LO01.title: Solve equations involving more than one operation
LO01.prepare: Undo operations in reverse order: first add/subtract, then multiply/divide. Check by substituting. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO02.title: Translate sentences into equations
LO02.prepare: Translate word by word: “is” means =, “of” means ×, “more than” adds, “less than” subtracts in reverse order. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO03.title: Solve equations with the variable on each side
LO03.prepare: Collect the variable terms on one side and the constants on the other, then divide. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO04.title: Solve absolute value equations
LO04.prepare: Isolate |A| = b. If b > 0 solve A = b and A = −b; if b < 0 there is no solution. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO05.title: Find the slope of a line
LO05.prepare: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); a horizontal line has slope 0 and a vertical line has undefined slope. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO06.title: Solve proportions
LO06.prepare: a/b = c/d ⇒ ad = bc (cross products), then solve. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO07.title: Graph and interpret linear functions
LO07.prepare: Use intercepts and slope to describe and graph a line; interpret them in the context. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO08.title: Apply translations to absolute value functions
LO08.prepare: y = |x − h| + k moves the vertex of |x| to (h, k). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO09.title: Graph the solutions of an inequality
LO09.prepare: Closed dot for ≤ or ≥, open dot for < or >; shade the side that makes the inequality true. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO10.title: Construct arithmetic sequences
LO10.prepare: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d, where d is the common difference. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO11.title: Solve linear inequalities involving more than one operation
LO11.prepare: Solve like an equation; reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO12.title: Solve and graph absolute value inequalities (<)
LO12.prepare: |A| < b (b > 0) means −b < A < b: a single interval between two values. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO13.title: Apply dilations to linear functions
LO13.prepare: g(x) = a·f(x) stretches vertically if |a| > 1, compresses if 0 < |a| < 1, reflects if a < 0. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO14.title: Write equations of lines in point-slope form given two points
LO14.prepare: Find m from the two points, then y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO15.title: Create and identify equations of parallel or perpendicular lines
LO15.prepare: Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular slopes multiply to −1. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO16.title: Construct the inverses of relations
LO16.prepare: Swap x and y in every pair (or in the equation) to get the inverse relation. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO17.title: Identify and graph piecewise-defined functions
LO17.prepare: Graph each piece only on its interval; closed dot where the endpoint is included (≤, ≥), open dot where it is not. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO18.title: Identify and graph step functions
LO18.prepare: ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer ≤ x; each step has a closed left end and an open right end. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO19.title: Graph absolute value functions
LO19.prepare: y = a|x − h| + k: vertex (h, k), opens up if a > 0, down if a < 0, |a| changes the width. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO20.title: Write a line in slope-intercept form given slope and one point
LO20.prepare: Substitute the point and slope in y = mx + b to find b. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO21.title: Solve and graph compound inequalities with AND; solve equations using distribution
LO21.prepare: “And”: the solution is the intersection (overlap) of both inequalities. For equations, distribute first, then collect terms. Enter the data in STATISTICS and read the mean, deviation and quartiles; describe shape from the graph yourself.

LO22.title: Graph linear functions using x- and y-intercepts
LO22.prepare: x-intercept: set y = 0; y-intercept: set x = 0; plot both and draw the line. Read key features from the graph, or build a TABLE of values to plot and compare.

LO23.title: Create and identify equations of parallel or perpendicular lines
LO23.prepare: Write each line as y = mx + b and compare slopes: equal ⇒ parallel, product −1 ⇒ perpendicular. Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO24.title: Apply the arithmetic sequence formula
LO24.prepare: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d; graph the terms as separate points (n, aₙ). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.

LO25.title: Solve equations for specific variables
LO25.prepare: Isolate the requested variable using inverse operations; state real-world constraints (non-negative whole numbers, budget). Draw or read the diagram first, set up the ratio or formula by hand, then calculate.
